item.title: Guardians drop Cactus League game to Rangers, 11-4
item.description: The Rangers got to non-roster invitee Codi Heuer for five runs in the fourth inning, and Texas rolled to an 11-4 victory over the Guardians on Feb. 25. Heuer faced six batters, got one out, gave up five hits and two walks. All five runs were earned. Slade Cecconi started and went two scoreless innings. He gave up two hits and struck out one. item.title: Cleveland State men drop sixth in a row, 81-70, to Northern Kentucky
item.description: Northern Kentucky made the Cleveland State men pay on Tim Misny bobblehead night. The Norse jumped to a double-digit lead in the first seven minutes of the game and cruised to an 87-70 victory in front of 2,458 at the Wolstein Center. The Vikings (10-20, 6-13 Horizon) have lost six in a row. Ryan Priest scored 20 points for Cleveland State, which made only 5 of 24 3-pointers. item.title: Monsters rally from two-goal deficit to beat Rochester, 4-2
item.description: After spotting Rochester a two-goal lead in the first period, the Monsters blanked the Americans the rest of the way and won, 4-2, on Feb. 25 at Rocket Arena. Zach Aston-Reese, Luca Marrelli, James Malatesta and Mikael Pyyhtiä each scored a goal for the Monsters (27-16-6-1), who have won three in a row. item.title: Mentor vs. Lorain girls basketball: Cardinals’ pressure takes Titans out early
item.description: Conventional wisdom — and sports cliche — says it’s tough to beat a team three times in a season. The Mentor girls basketball team — well — the Cardinals aren’t conventional. Utilizing a smothering full-court press, Mentor led visiting Lorain, 7-0, before the Titans were able to finally get the ball across halfcourt. item.title: Short-handed Cavaliers fall to Bucks, 118-116, in Milwaukee
item.description: By JIM HOEHN MILWAUKEE — Kevin Porter Jr. had 20 points, Ryan Rollins added 18 and the Bucks held off the short-handed Cavaliers, 118-116, on Feb. 25 for their fifth victory in six games. The Cavaliers appeared to tie it on Jarrett Allen’s basket underneath at the buzzer, but it was ruled that time had expired. Allen had 27 points and 11 rebounds.
